content:
maria: quick thread, ran a focused bakeoff: "stabilized activation scaling" (SAS) + 2-stage quant (AWQ -> GPTQ-refit) on archimedes-7b at 64k context. TL;DR: latency improves ~8-12% vs AWQ-only at same batch, quality loss smaller than AWQ-only (avg= -1.6% vs -3.4% on our long-context summarization suite). detailed notes below.
ajay: can you attach the exact configs + eval scripts?
maria: pasted the commands I used for reproducibility: ```bash
# AWQ stage with SAS transforms
python tools/quantize.py --model archimedes-7b --ctx 65536 --method awq
  --act-transform stabilized --bits 4 --block-size 128
  --out ./artifacts/arch_awq_sas.pt

# GPTQ refit to shave accuracy loss
python tools/gptq_refit.py --input ./artifacts/arch_awq_sas.pt
  --refit-lr 1e-4 --steps 800 --calib dataset/longctx_calib.json
  --out ./artifacts/arch_awq_sas_refit.pt
```
maria: eval harness: `python eval/longctx_suite.py --model ./artifacts/arch_awq_sas_refit.pt --tasks summarization,qa --seed 42`
tess: any KV cache oddities? longctx can expose act-scale drift.
maria: saw a small KV-cache warmup mismatch on first 2k tokens where throughput dropped ~20% until cache warmed; added small prefix cache priming reduced the dip. logs: ```
[INFO] kv_cache: priming 2048 tokens -> peak_mem 21.3GB -> steady 18.7GB
[WARN] kv_cache: first-epoch misses=0.12 -> priming reduced to 0.03
```
oliver: did you try layerwise FP16 for the first few layers? keeping early layers higher precision often helps with activation distribution.
maria: yes, ran layerwise-fp16=0..3. results: quality regained ~0.9% (MRR/ROUGE) compared to pure SAS+AWQ, latency +4% and VRAM +2GB. tradeoff looks good for canary.
ajay: curious about regressions on instruction-following tests — any catastrophic failures?
maria: no catastrophic failures. most regressions are subtle phrasing and hallucination upticks on very long chains (>=20 hops). we flagged 12 prompts for manual review; sample diffs attached in the workspace.
ci-bot: perf-run finished: p95 latency baseline FP8=184ms, AWQ-only=168ms, SAS+AWQ=155ms, SAS+AWQ+refit=160ms; token throughput improved 9% at batch=8.
ryan: for rollout I'd recommend: 1) deploy SAS+AWQ+refit to Dedicated canary (10% traffic) 2) enable prefix priming cache for first 10s of requests 3) monitor MRR/ROUGE and APDEX, auto-fallback to FP8 baseline above 2% regression window.
maria: +1. I'll open a canary run ticket and include the exact artifacts & eval diffs. tagging @ajay @tess for follow-up on manual examples. :thumbsup:
